problem_markdown: A convex $n$-gon, $n>3$, has perimeter $p$ and total diagonal length $d$. Prove $n-3<2d/p<\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor-2$.
solutions_markdown:
Number vertices cyclically. For each diagonal $A_iA_j$, the shifted diagonal $A_{i+1}A_{j+1}$ crosses it. Splitting at their intersection and applying triangle inequalities gives
$$|A_iA_j|+|A_{i+1}A_{j+1}|>|A_iA_{i+1}|+|A_jA_{j+1}|.$$
Sum over all oriented diagonals. Each diagonal length appears four times and each side $2(n-3)$ times, so $4d>2(n-3)p$.

For the upper bound, the sum over $i$ of chords $|A_iA_{i+r}|$ is strictly less than $rp$, by comparing each chord with its $r$-side boundary arc.

If $n=2m+1$, taking $r=2,\ldots,m$ counts every diagonal once. Hence $d<\sum_{r=2}^m rp=[m(m+1)/2-1]p$.

If $n=2m$, take $r=2,\ldots,m-1$ for the nonopposite diagonals. Each of the $m$ opposite-vertex diagonals is shorter than either half-boundary arc and therefore shorter than $p/2$. Thus $d<[\sum_{r=2}^{m-1}r+m/2]p=(m^2/2-1)p$. These are exactly the stated upper bounds.
